prompt.7-10: Find the verse that says you can do all things through Christ.
prompt.11-14: Find the verse where Paul says he can do all things through Christ who strengthens him.
prompt.15-18: Find Paul's statement about strength for all things — and read the two verses before it.

prompt.7-10: Find the verse about God loving the world so much.
prompt.11-14: Find the verse that begins 'For God so loved the world'.
prompt.15-18: Find the verse most often quoted about God's love — then read verse 17 with it.

prompt.7-10: Find the psalm that starts 'The Lord is my shepherd'.
prompt.11-14: Find the psalm that begins with a shepherd. Which number is it?
prompt.15-18: Find the shepherd psalm and note where the pronouns change from 'he' to 'you'.

prompt.7-10: Find the very first verse in the Bible.
prompt.11-14: Find the first verse of the Bible — book, chapter and verse.
prompt.15-18: Find the Bible's opening line and notice what it does not argue for.

prompt.7-10: Find where Jesus says 'You are the light of the world'.
prompt.11-14: Find where Jesus calls his followers the light of the world.
prompt.15-18: Find the light-of-the-world saying inside the Sermon on the Mount.

prompt.7-10: Find the verse about trusting God with all your heart.
prompt.11-14: Find the proverb about trusting the Lord with all your heart.
prompt.15-18: Find the proverb that tells you not to lean on your own understanding.

prompt.7-10: Find the verse that says God works things together for good.
prompt.11-14: Find where Paul says God works all things together for good.
prompt.15-18: Find Romans' 'all things work together' verse and note who it is addressed to.

prompt.7-10: Find where God tells Joshua to be strong and brave.
prompt.11-14: Find God's command to Joshua to be strong and courageous.
prompt.15-18: Find Joshua's commissioning command and count how often it is repeated in that chapter.

prompt.7-10: Find the verse where God says 'do not fear, I am with you'.
prompt.11-14: Find Isaiah's 'do not fear, for I am with you'.
prompt.15-18: Find Isaiah 41's fear-not oracle and note the grounds it gives.

prompt.7-10: Find the verse that says we love because God loved us first.
prompt.11-14: Find where John says we love because he first loved us.
prompt.15-18: Find John's statement on the priority of divine love.

prompt.7-10: Can you say your memory verse without looking?
prompt.11-14: Write out your memory verse from memory, then check it.
prompt.15-18: Write out your current memory verse from memory, then check it word by word.

prompt.7-10: Say your memory verse out loud to someone in your family.
prompt.11-14: Say your memory verse out loud to someone — out loud is harder than in your head.
prompt.15-18: Recite your memory verse aloud to someone. Speaking it tests it differently from writing it.

prompt.7-10: Can you remember which book your memory verse comes from?
prompt.11-14: Can you say your memory verse and its reference?
prompt.15-18: Recite your verse with its reference, and say in one sentence what the passage around it is doing.

prompt.7-10: Practise your memory verse three times today.
prompt.11-14: Review your memory verse three times today — morning, afternoon and evening.
prompt.15-18: Space three reviews of your verse across today rather than doing them together.

prompt.7-10: How many books are in the whole Bible?
prompt.11-14: How many books are in the Bible?
prompt.15-18: How many books are in the Protestant canon?

explain.7-10: 39 in the Old Testament and 27 in the New Testament — 66 altogether.
explain.11-14: 39 in the Old Testament plus 27 in the New makes 66.
explain.15-18: 66 in the Protestant canon; Catholic and Orthodox canons include additional books.

prompt.7-10: Who was thrown into the lions' den?
prompt.11-14: Who was thrown into the lions' den?
prompt.15-18: Who was thrown into the lions' den, and under which king?

explain.7-10: Daniel — and God kept the lions' mouths shut.
explain.11-14: Daniel, for praying when a new law forbade it.
explain.15-18: Daniel, under Darius — the point of the story is the immovability of the law, not the king's malice.

prompt.7-10: What did God make on the first day?
prompt.11-14: What did God create on the first day?
prompt.15-18: What is created on day one of Genesis 1?

explain.11-14: Light — before the sun, which comes on day four.
explain.15-18: Light on day one, luminaries on day four — a structure that demotes the sun and moon from deities to lamps.

prompt.7-10: Who baptised Jesus?
prompt.11-14: Who baptised Jesus in the Jordan?
prompt.15-18: Who baptised Jesus, and what did he say about it?

explain.7-10: John the Baptist, in the River Jordan.
explain.11-14: John the Baptist, who said he was not worthy to untie Jesus' sandals.
explain.15-18: John, who protested that the order should be reversed — Matthew alone records the exchange.

prompt.7-10: How many disciples did Jesus choose?
prompt.11-14: How many disciples did Jesus choose?
prompt.15-18: How many were in the inner circle Jesus appointed?

explain.11-14: Twelve — one for each tribe of Israel.
explain.15-18: Twelve, a deliberate echo of the tribes and a claim about the renewal of Israel.

prompt.7-10: What did David use to fight Goliath?
prompt.11-14: What did David take into the fight with Goliath?
prompt.15-18: What did David take against Goliath, and what did he refuse?

explain.7-10: A sling and five smooth stones.
explain.11-14: A sling and five smooth stones from the stream — he turned down Saul's armour.
explain.15-18: A sling and five stones, having refused Saul's armour — the refusal is the theological point.

prompt.7-10: Who was swallowed by a big fish?
prompt.11-14: Who was swallowed by a great fish?
prompt.15-18: Who was swallowed by a great fish, and where was he running to?

explain.7-10: Jonah, when he ran away from God.
explain.11-14: Jonah, running from God's call to Nineveh.
explain.15-18: Jonah, sailing for Tarshish — the opposite direction from Nineveh.

prompt.7-10: Which book comes first in the New Testament?
prompt.11-14: Which book opens the New Testament?
prompt.15-18: Which gospel stands first in the canonical order?

explain.11-14: Matthew — though Mark was probably written first.
explain.15-18: Matthew stands first canonically; most scholars hold Mark to be the earliest written.

prompt.7-10: Who said he did not know Jesus three times?
prompt.11-14: Who denied Jesus three times?
prompt.15-18: Who denied Jesus three times, and how was he restored?

explain.7-10: Peter — and Jesus forgave him afterwards.
explain.15-18: Peter, restored by a threefold question on the shore in John 21.

prompt.7-10: Which queen was brave for her people?
prompt.11-14: Which queen risked her life to save her people?
prompt.15-18: Which queen intervened for her people at personal risk?

explain.7-10: Esther, who went to see the king without being invited.
explain.15-18: Esther, in a book that never once names God — the providence is structural rather than stated.

prompt.7-10: What is the first commandment Jesus said is the biggest?
prompt.11-14: What did Jesus say the greatest commandment is?
prompt.15-18: What did Jesus name as the greatest commandment?

options: Love God with all your heart

explain.7-10: Love God with everything you are — and love other people too.
explain.11-14: Love God with all your heart, soul, mind and strength; and love your neighbour as yourself.
explain.15-18: Deuteronomy 6:5 joined to Leviticus 19:18 — the joining is what makes the answer distinctive.

prompt.7-10: How many days was Jesus in the tomb?
prompt.11-14: How long was Jesus in the tomb?
prompt.15-18: How is the length of Jesus' burial described?

explain.7-10: Three days — he rose on Sunday.
explain.11-14: Three days: Friday evening to Sunday morning.
explain.15-18: Reckoned inclusively in Jewish counting — part of Friday, Saturday, and part of Sunday.

prompt.7-10: Who is someone you find it hard to be kind to? Why?
prompt.11-14: Who do you find it hardest to be kind to, and what makes it hard?
prompt.15-18: Who do you find it hardest to be generous towards, and what does that reveal?

prompt.7-10: What is the biggest thing you have to be thankful for today?
prompt.11-14: What are you grateful for that you usually do not notice?
prompt.15-18: What good thing in your life have you started treating as ordinary?

prompt.7-10: When was the last time you were brave?
prompt.11-14: When did you last do the right thing when it was not easy?
prompt.15-18: When did you last act on a conviction that cost you something?

prompt.7-10: What do you want to ask God about?
prompt.11-14: What question about God have you not asked out loud?
prompt.15-18: What question about faith are you carrying that you have not said aloud to anyone?

prompt.7-10: Who could you say sorry to?
prompt.11-14: Is there someone you owe an apology to?
prompt.15-18: Where do you owe an apology that pride has been postponing?

prompt.7-10: What is your 'Goliath' at the moment?
prompt.11-14: What feels too big for you right now?
prompt.15-18: What are you facing that you would rather not name?

prompt.7-10: What makes you feel close to God?
prompt.11-14: When do you feel closest to God, and when furthest?
prompt.15-18: What practices actually change you, and which are habit without effect?

prompt.7-10: If Jesus came to your school, who do you think he would sit with?
prompt.11-14: Who at your school gets overlooked? What would Jesus do about it?
prompt.15-18: Who is on the edge of your circles, and what would including them actually cost you?

prompt.7-10: What is one thing you could do for someone in your family today?
prompt.11-14: What does your family need from you this week that nobody has asked for?
prompt.15-18: What responsibility have you been leaving to someone else at home?

prompt.7-10: What are you scared of? Have you told God?
prompt.11-14: What are you afraid of at the moment? Have you prayed about it honestly?
prompt.15-18: What fear are you managing rather than facing?

prompt.7-10: Say something kind to someone today and do not wait for a thank you.
prompt.11-14: Encourage someone today without expecting anything back.
prompt.15-18: Encourage someone today with no expectation of return — and do not mention it afterwards.

prompt.7-10: Do a job at home without being asked.
prompt.11-14: Do something helpful at home today without being asked or mentioning it.
prompt.15-18: Do something useful today that nobody will know you did.

prompt.7-10: Ask a friend how they really are.
prompt.11-14: Ask someone how they actually are — and stay for the answer.
prompt.15-18: Ask someone how they are and stay past the first, polite answer.

prompt.7-10: Forgive someone in your head today.
prompt.11-14: Let go of one thing you have been holding against someone.
prompt.15-18: Take a step towards forgiving something you have been rehearsing.

prompt.7-10: Listen to someone all the way to the end without interrupting.

prompt.15-18: Do one piece of work today to a standard nobody is checking for.

prompt.7-10: Say thank you to someone who helps you every day.
prompt.11-14: Thank someone who does something for you that you normally take for granted.
prompt.15-18: Thank someone specifically — name the thing — who is used to being unthanked.
